**4.7 Common Issue Examples**

To assist with training and future process improvements, representative examples from each major
category are listed below. Ticket IDs have been anonymised to protect customer data, but the
underlying pattern is described.

- **Password reset (TKT-2214):** Customer was unable to log in after a browser update. The
  password was reset via the standard verification flow, and the customer was advised to clear
  cached credentials. No further action required.
- **Billing query (TKT-2248):** Customer noticed a duplicate charge for the monthly subscription.
  The finance team confirmed a processing error on 11 May and issued a refund within three business
  days. The refund reference was shared with the customer.
- **Technical fault (TKT-2271):** Customer reported that the mobile application crashed on launch
  after the latest update. The issue was traced to a corrupted local cache; clearing the cache
  resolved the problem. A note was added to the release notes for the next version.
- **Account update (TKT-2305):** Customer requested a change of registered mobile number. The
  update was completed after OTP verification. The customer confirmed that the new number was
  working correctly.
- **Feature request (TKT-2332):** Customer requested an option to export transaction history in
  CSV format. The request was logged and forwarded to the product team for the roadmap. The
  customer was informed that this is under consideration for a future release.
- **Complaint (service) (TKT-2350):** Customer reported that a support agent was unhelpful during
  a previous interaction. The call recording was reviewed, and the concerned agent was given
  additional coaching. The customer was contacted directly by the Team Lead and offered an
  apology.

The survey responses received during May 2026 included several open-ended comments. A recurring
theme was appreciation for quick resolution of password and billing issues. A smaller number of
respondents mentioned that the hold time on the phone line was longer than expected on weekday
afternoons. The average hold time for the month was 3 minutes 40 seconds, which is within the

**4.9 Escalations**

A total of 12 tickets were escalated to a higher support tier during May 2026. Of these, 9 were
technical faults that required infrastructure team involvement, 2 were billing disputes that
needed finance approval, and 1 was a feature request that was escalated to the product manager
for a prioritisation decision.
